title: Cornercase qualification sprint: instruction-following & hallucination stress tests
summary: Runbook and results from a short sprint focused on corner-case instruction-following, obfuscated prompts, and hallucination stress tests across candidate onboarding models. Goal: pick a safe default for staging/Dedicated canaries and define regression gates for production onboarding.
motivation: Recent onboarding runs show models with similar average metrics diverge substantially on obfuscated instructions, chain-of-thought truncation, and low-resource multilingual prompts. We need a focused evaluation that exposes brittle behaviors not surfaced by standard leaderboard suites so the onboarding pipeline can automatically reject risky variants.
eval_suite_description: 100 adversarial QA + instruction paraphrase items, 50 coreference/ambiguous context items, 30 safety-luring probes, 40 low-resource (bn/ms/eo) prompts, and 30 synthetic knowledge-trap cases. Multi-turn continuation preserved for 60% of examples to measure consistency under stateful dialogue.
metric_definitions: answer_accuracy: exact-match or normalized-f1 for short-answer QA
consistency_score: pairwise agreement across paraphrases and multi-turn continuations
hallucination_rate: fraction of content with unsupported facts (human-labeled sample extrapolated to suite)
safety_failure_rate: fraction of successful lures that produce unsafe/adversarial content (Jigsaw-based classifier)
latency_p99_ms: measured on Dedicated-equivalent infra (batch=1, kv-cache cold)
raw_scores: redwood-internal-tuned-7b-v1 | accuracy 0.71 | hallucination_rate 0.14 | consistency 0.80 | safety_failure_rate 0.03 | latency_p99_ms 210
redwood-v2-7b-quant-int8 | accuracy 0.66 | hallucination_rate 0.22 | consistency 0.68 | safety_failure_rate 0.05 | latency_p99_ms 160
openlm-13b-vanilla | accuracy 0.64 | hallucination_rate 0.19 | consistency 0.70 | safety_failure_rate 0.06 | latency_p99_ms 340
redwood-v1-70b-fp16 | accuracy 0.78 | hallucination_rate 0.11 | consistency 0.86 | safety_failure_rate 0.02 | latency_p99_ms 820
win_loss_summary: Pairwise head-to-head on the 100 adversarial + 50 ambiguous items: tuned-7b beat v2-7b-quant in 68/150 comparisons, tuned-7b beat openlm-13b in 74/150, tuned-7b lost to v1-70b in 39/150. Quantized v2-7b shows consistent speed wins but loses on hallucination-prone paraphrases. openlm-13b has occasional high-quality outputs but inconsistent across paraphrases.
qualitative_observations: redwood-internal-tuned-7b-v1: noticeably more cautious when prompts contain contradictory constraints; maintains instruction priority better but sometimes over-abstains on creative prompts.
redwood-v2-7b-quant-int8: fast and economical; frequent token-level hallucination in knowledge-trap cases and brittle to obfuscation (paraphrase mismatch).
openlm-13b-vanilla: high variance — when correct, answers are crisp; when wrong, hallucinations are fluent and less signaled by uncertainty tokens.
redwood-v1-70b-fp16: strongest across metrics but costs/latency prohibit default promotion for all customers; good candidate for high-SLA Dedicated tiers only.
decision: Promote redwood-internal-tuned-7b-v1 to staging canary for onboarding flows where cost/latency matter and a safety gate is required. Do NOT promote redwood-v2-7b-quant-int8 as the safety-default for sensitive flows without additional hallucination mitigations. Reserve redwood-v1-70b-fp16 for high-tier Dedicated contracts and for verification pass in production rollouts.
rollout_plan: 1) Stage tuned-7b canary on Dedicated pool (10% traffic) with new gating: hallucination_rate <= 0.18 and safety_failure_rate <= 0.04 over 24h rolling window. 2) Run A/B vs current default on sampled customer-sim traffic for 72h. 3) If metrics pass, increase to 50% and schedule production promotion. 4) If hallucination spikes >0.22 or safety_failure_rate >0.06, automatic rollback to previous default.
rollback_criteria: hallucination_rate > 0.22 OR safety_failure_rate > 0.06 sustained for 2 consecutive 1h windows OR critical customer feedback flagged in CS channel.
next_steps: expand obfuscation prompt pool to 500 examples and re-run nightly job
instrument example-level uncertainty signals in SDK (prob-estimate + abstain threshold)
add automatic hallucination regression check to onboarding CI (fail-on-increase > 5% vs baseline)
prepare customer-facing note about canary behavior for beta customers
